clue.text: Disposing of item of food that's left abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned says the letter for left is dropped from the food word

parts.note: a dumpling is an item of food

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a scrap of food left lying around.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumping something is getting rid of it, a synonym of disposing of it.

clue.text: Author held up novel at last

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: held means had, as in held or had possession

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word novel

explanation.surface: A writer was delayed with a novel until the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for held, as this is a down clue. Roald Dahl wrote children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl is a famous author, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: By the sound of it, failed to see a proper version of An Ideal Husband?

indicators.note: this phrase says the words are to be spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: failed to see a is 'missed a', which said quickly sounds like mister
proper means right, as in the right or correct way

explanation.surface: A punning take on Oscar Wilde's play about the perfect spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed a' is pronounced like 'mister', written MR. The printed grid answer MCRIGHT is a misreading of MR RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the idiom for the perfect partner a woman hopes to marry.

clue.text: Minor publication that is appearing without picture

indicators.note: appearing without means the letters for that is sit on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a mag is a magazine, a small-scale publication

explanation.surface: A small magazine is printed with no illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: 'appearing without' puts the abbreviation round the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: I don't believe you manage

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, like 'come off it'

explanation.definitionFit: Get along is both a cry of incredulity and a phrase for coping or getting by.

clue.text: Was busy reorganising transport systems

indicators.note: reorganising tells us to rearrange the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone was busy restructuring the city's public transport network.
explanation.definitionFit: Subways are underground railways or pedestrian tunnels, both kinds of transport system.

clue.text: Posh, pale blue clothes

indicators.note: clothes used as a verb, meaning dresses or wraps around something

parts.note: the sky is blue, so blue gives sky
wan means pale

explanation.surface: Smart garments in a light blue shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb meaning wraps around, not garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Swanky means stylishly showy and expensive, a synonym of posh.

clue.text: A Schubert composition is capital

indicators.note: composition suggests the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A piece of music by Schubert is described as first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges ASCHUBERT. 'capital' looks like the adjective meaning excellent; it is a noun, a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania, a definition by example.

clue.text: Seafood sailor has without anything else

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common crossword sailor
alone means by itself, with nothing else

explanation.surface: A sailor has only seafood to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail, a kind of shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Telephone unlikely, to pose a risk for criminal

parts.note: something safe is unlikely to be dangerous
blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: A phone call is unlikely to endanger a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the telephone word may sit below the safety word; blower is old British slang for the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe-blower is a criminal who uses explosives to break open safes.

clue.text: Curry dish mostly served in here with a hot drink

indicators.note: served in means one piece is placed inside the word here

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly removes the final letter of the curry word

parts.note: a balti is a curry dish cooked in a metal pan
taken as written

explanation.surface: A curry is mostly eaten here with a cup of something hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the curry's last letter, and 'served in' sets the rest within the word here. A balti is a curry style popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbal tea is an infusion of herbs drunk hot, an example of a hot drink.

clue.text: Light-hearted banter? Shucks

definitions.meaning: husks or pods stripped from grain or seeds

explanation.definitionFit: Chaff means both playful teasing and the husks separated from grain.

clue.text: Performs exceptionally well, and has explosive effect

definitions.meaning: British idiom for being a great success or going very fast
literally behaving like a detonating device

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to succeed hugely, and literally describes something blowing up.

clue.text: Sketch featuring hooligan conscript

parts.note: a rough is a violent hooligan
to draft is to conscript into military service

explanation.surface: A comic sketch about a thug who is called up to the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough draft is a preliminary sketch or outline of a piece of work.

clue.text: Leaving unacceptable limit

parts.note: out means not acceptable, as in that idea is out
a bound is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: Departing beyond what is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Outbound means heading away, so departing or leaving.

clue.text: Award is not initially accepted by one showing deference

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch
taken as written

indicators.note: accepted by means a letter is taken inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one on a playing card or die

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word not

explanation.surface: Someone shows respect though their honour was never received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letter of 'not', which 'accepted by' puts inside the word for one. The OBE is an Order of the British Empire honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a gesture of respect or homage, a synonym of deference.

clue.text: Ban tours round northeastern region of Italy

indicators.note: tours round means the ban word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a veto is a ban
NE is the abbreviation for northeast

explanation.surface: Restrictions on travel around a part of northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ban' looks like a verb but is a noun; 'tours round' wraps it around the compass abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneto is the region of northeast Italy whose capital is Venice.

clue.text: Blue books turned up about end of last century? Rubbish

indicators.note: about means the reversed pieces go around the others
in a down clue, turned up means the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory
OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible
MM is two thousand in Roman numerals, the final year of the twentieth century

explanation.surface: Conservative books turned upside down around the millennium, nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses Tory plus the Bible books together, giving TOYROT, and 'about' puts 2000 in Roman numerals inside. Tories are 'blues' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot is an old-fashioned word for nonsense, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Blush, having eaten first bit of gateau, wolfed greedily

indicators.note: having eaten means the blush phrase swallows the next piece

parts.note: to blush is to go red

indicators.note: first bit of picks the opening letter of gateau

explanation.surface: Someone turns red after eating some cake, having gobbled it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blush' is GO RED, which takes in G from 'gateau'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to eat greedily, so gorged means wolfed down.

clue.text: Play guitar, with leading characters in rock opera on stage

indicators.note: leading characters picks the first letter of each of the next words

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar casually

explanation.surface: A musician plays guitar during a rock opera on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker, so a stage.

clue.text: Noisily disapprove of wood in shop

indicators.note: noisily signals the words are to be spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: to disapprove is to boo, and teak is a wood

explanation.surface: Jeering at timber in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: BOO plus TEAK said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable shop.

clue.text: One may put down strange lines being penned

indicators.note: being penned means enclosed, so the lines go inside the strange word

parts.note: queer means strange
L is a line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Strange lines are written by someone who suppresses things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing but means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A queller suppresses or crushes something, such as one who puts down a revolt.

clue.text: Leaves bags in here?

parts.note: read as tea leaves and tea bags going into a vessel for brewing, not someone departing

explanation.definitionFit: Loose tea leaves and teabags are put into this brewing vessel.

clue.text: Madly admires Soviet film

indicators.note: madly suggests the letters of the following words are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is wildly enthusiastic about a Soviet movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster movie is a genre of film about catastrophes.

clue.text: Circular letter received by deputy speaker

indicators.note: received by means the round letter is taken inside the deputy word

parts.note: vice, as in vice-president, means deputy
O is the round letter

explanation.surface: A circular is accepted by the assistant to the Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular letter' suggests a mailing; it is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice can mean a person who speaks for others, a spokesperson.

clue.text: Getting involved in party politics is a mistake

indicators.note: getting involved in says the answer is tucked inside the following words

explanation.surface: Joining party politics is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing or printing error, so a mistake.

clue.text: See a pair on garment?

explanation.surface: Look at a couple wearing an item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a protective garment worn over clothes.

clue.text: Role, one taken by friend to a limited extent

indicators.note: taken by says the one is followed by the friend word

parts.note: a part is a role in a play
I is the Roman numeral for one
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: An actor's part is given to a friend only in part.
explanation.definitionFit: Partially means in part, so to a limited extent.

clue.text: Office worker's brief estimate creates a storm

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
EST is the short form of estimate

explanation.surface: A temporary office worker's quick guess causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm.

clue.text: Gold and black inlaid in the old instrument

indicators.note: inlaid in means the gold and black pieces are set inside the others

parts.note: taken as written
or is gold in heraldry
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Gold and black decoration set into an antique musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold here is the heraldic term; 'inlaid in' sets gold and black within 'the' plus the old abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorbo is a large bass lute, a stringed musical instrument.
